observed: §18.3.4 says 'the printed 600 ms' for the 4-bit GGUF tier, but §18.3.2's table prints 800 ms for that row, and §18.3.3 also uses 800 ms ('The 4-bit GGUF tier (800 ms)'). The 600 ms value appears only in §18.8's mini-case, which is a later, explicitly different scenario.
evidence: §18.3.2 table: '70B 4-bit GGUF | $0.15 | 800 | energy only'. §18.3.3: 'The 4-bit GGUF tier (800 ms)'. §18.3.4: '~200× the printed 600 ms'. §18.8: 'Tier 1 (4-bit GGUF): ... latency ~600 ms' and 'the 4-bit tier's ~600 ms latency differs from the ledger's 800 ms'.
root_cause: Forward reference to the mini-case's 600 ms value mislabeled as 'the printed' value; the §18.3.2 ledger prints 800 ms.
correction: Change 'the printed 600 ms' to 'the printed 800 ms' (or 'the mini-case's 600 ms') and recompute the multiple: 117 s / 0.8 s ≈ 146×, not ~200×.
acceptance_test: The multiple in §18.3.4 must match the latency value it cites; if 800 ms is cited, the multiple must be ~146×, not ~200×.

observed: §18.3.1 explicitly concludes that 70B dense 8-bit on 1×H100 holds only ~10 GB KV headroom against the 24.9 GB one canonical 9,500-token request needs — 'zero concurrent canonical requests' — and that the tier 'needs ≥2 GPUs'. The mini-case's Tier 2 runs on 1×H100 without reconciling this.
evidence: §18.3.1: '70B dense 8-bit on 1×H100 holds ~10 GB of KV headroom ... 10/24.89 = 0.40, i.e. zero concurrent canonical requests; the tier needs ≥2 GPUs'. §18.8: 'Tier 2 (70B 8-bit dense): ... Runs on 1×H100.'
root_cause: The mini-case's requests are ~250 tokens (not canonical 9.5K), so 1×H100 is feasible for its short requests — but the mini-case never states this reconciliation, leaving an apparent contradiction with §18.3.1.
correction: Add a sentence to §18.8's Tier 2: 'Unlike the canonical 9.5K case (§18.3.1), these ~250-token requests need only ~0.66 GB KV each, so 1×H100's ~10 GB headroom holds ~15 concurrent requests.'
acceptance_test: The mini-case must explicitly reconcile its 1×H100 placement with §18.3.1's ≥2-GPU finding for canonical requests.

quoted_clause: W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s ... ~14.16 s with prefix reuse ... ~14.16 s
observed: The text derives W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s from the stated 100%-prefix-reuse policy (incremental prefix 9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600), but the same section and Table 19-1 print ~14.16 s. The 14.16 value corresponds to using 11,795 (the full retained context) instead of 11,600.
root_cause: Two different prefix-reuse assumptions (11,600 incremental vs 11,795 full retained) are used in different places without reconciliation.
correction: Unify on the stated policy (11,600 incremental prefix) and change all 14.16 values to 14.14, or explicitly state that the table uses the full retained context and change the text's 14.14 to 14.16.
acceptance_test: The W_reuse(3) value must be identical in §19.4 prose, §19.4 summary, and Table 19-1, and must be reproducible from the stated prefix-reuse assumption.

quoted_clause: queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s
observed: The formula in the same sentence says 'buffer depth D·(200−r) requests' = 1 × (200−50) = 150 requests, and 'max queue wait ≈ D·(200−r)/r' = 1 × 150/50 = 3 s. The worked example instead uses 200 requests and ~4 s, which is the total arrivals and total drain time, not the excess buffer and max queue wait.
evidence: §23.8: 'max queue wait ≈ D·(200−r)/r must stay inside the 3 s SLO — so state D, the buffer depth D·(200−r) requests ... worked: D = 1 s at 200 rps → queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s'.
root_cause: Confusion between total arrivals (200) and excess buffer (150), and between total drain time (4 s) and max queue wait (3 s).
correction: Change 'queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s' to 'buffer depth 1 × (200−50) = 150 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~3 s'.
acceptance_test: The worked example's buffer depth and drain time must match the formula D·(200−r) and D·(200−r)/r stated in the same sentence.

quoted_clause: 40 rps × 8.6 s = 344 in-flight × 24.9 GB ÷ 436 GB = 19.7 → 21 hosts (Ch 17)
observed: The arithmetic yields 19.65 (printed as 19.7), but the result is stated as 21 hosts. A clean ceil of 19.7 is 20, not 21. The FP8 analogue later in the same chapter explicitly writes '+N−1' (9.8 + 1 → 11), but this FP16 line omits the +N−1 step, so the reader cannot see how 19.7 becomes 21.
evidence: 344 × 24.9 = 8565.6; 8565.6 ÷ 436 = 19.65. ceil(19.65) = 20. To reach 21 requires an additional +1 (N−1) step: 19.65 + 1 = 20.65 → 21. The text does not state that step here, while it does state it in the FP8 calculation.
root_cause: The +N−1 policy step is applied implicitly in the FP16 line but explicitly in the FP8 line, creating an apparent arithmetic gap.
correction: Either write '19.7 + 1 (N−1) = 20.7 → 21 hosts' or add a parenthetical: '(19.7 raw + 1 N−1 reserve → 21)'. Match the FP8 line's explicit '+N−1' phrasing.
acceptance_test: The FP16 peak-KV line shows the +N−1 step explicitly, and 19.7 + 1 = 20.7 → 21 is arithmetically visible.

quoted_clause: samples 1,000 retrievals per cycle (n ≈ 1,000 sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; 0.001 resolution)
observed: With n=1,000 and a true rate near 0.3%, the expected event count is 3. The 95% binomial CI for 3/1,000 is roughly [0.06%, 0.88%], which is far wider than the 0.3% target. n=1,000 gives a 95% upper bound of 0.3% only in the zero-event case (rule of three: 3/1,000 = 0.003). The claim 'sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence' is therefore only true under a zero-failure observation, not in general.
evidence: For p=0.003, n=1,000: SE = sqrt(0.003×0.997/1,000) ≈ 0.00173; 95% CI half-width ≈ 0.0034. Zero-event 95% upper bound = 3/1,000 = 0.003. The '0.001 resolution' is the measurement granularity (1 event per 1,000), not the confidence-interval width.
root_cause: Conflating measurement granularity (0.001) with statistical confidence at the target rate.
correction: Rephrase: 'n ≈ 1,000 gives 0.001 measurement granularity and a 95% zero-event upper bound of 0.3%; detecting a true rate near 0.3% with a tight CI requires a larger n (e.g., ~3,000–4,000 for a ±0.1% half-width at p≈0.003).'
acceptance_test: The text distinguishes granularity from CI width and does not claim n=1,000 is sufficient to estimate a 0.3% rate with a tight 95% CI.

quoted_clause: However, two metrics remain above target: the false-positive rate at 2.4% ... and the guardrail-trigger rate at 5.4 per 1,000 (target <5); the poisoned-hit rate sits exactly at its ≈0.003 ceiling.
observed: The §4.1 table defines the poisoned-hit-rate target as '< 0.003'. A value of 0.003 is not < 0.003, so the poisoned-hit rate does not meet target. The mini-case counts only two metrics as 'above target' and treats the poisoned-hit rate as merely 'at its ceiling', implying it passes. Three metrics fail target at Cycle 2, not two.
evidence: Table 24-1 target column: 'Poisoned-hit rate | < 0.003'. Cycle 2 value: 0.003. 0.003 < 0.003 is false. The mini-case's own sentence says the rate 'sits exactly at its ≈0.003 ceiling' — i.e., at the boundary, not below it.
root_cause: Inconsistent treatment of the '<' operator: the table uses strict '<', but the mini-case prose treats 'at 0.003' as passing.
correction: Either (a) change the target to '≤ 0.003' in Table 24-1 and §4.1, or (b) rephrase the mini-case to say 'three metrics do not meet target: FP 2.4%, guardrail 5.4/1,000, and poisoned-hit 0.003 (at the <0.003 ceiling, not below it).'
acceptance_test: The mini-case and Table 24-1 agree on whether 0.003 meets the poisoned-hit target, and the count of failing metrics is consistent.

issue: The Token IDs box contains 'Integers order = position', which can be read as saying the integer token ID encodes or determines position. Token IDs are vocabulary indices; position is supplied separately by position IDs/positional encoding.
evidence: Figure 1.2: 'Token IDs / Integers / order = position'. The caption describes only 'text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention → KV cache' and does not define or justify 'order = position'.
acceptance_test: Replace with 'integer vocabulary IDs; sequence order gives position' or add a separate position input. Verify the figure no longer implies that the token-ID value itself encodes position.

issue: The arrow from Embedding to Attention is labelled 'attend'. Embeddings do not attend; attention consumes the embedded token and computes Q/K/V. The label misassigns the attention operation to the embedding-to-attention transition.
evidence: Figure 1.2 shows 'Embedding' → 'attend' → 'Attention'. The Attention box itself says 'Q,K,V (this token) vs all past tokens'. The caption says 'embedding → attention', not that embedding performs attention.
acceptance_test: Relabel the arrow 'project to Q/K/V' or 'input embeddings'. Verify the word 'attend' appears only on the attention operation or the KV-cache read path, not on the embedding output.

issue: The diagram shows Attention → 'append K,V' → KV Cache, which suggests attention produces or appends K/V after computing attention. In the transformer, K/V for the current token are computed by projection before attention uses them; attention reads cached K/V and the current K/V, and the current K/V are stored for future steps.
evidence: Figure 1.2: 'Attention' box → arrow 'append K,V' → 'KV Cache'. The caption itself warns: 'The K/V are produced within every applicable layer (not after a single "attention" stage)'. The drawn causal order still places append after the Attention box.
acceptance_test: Redraw so current-token K/V are produced before or alongside attention, with attention reading past K/V from cache plus current K/V, and the append/store path clearly storing current K/V for future steps. Verify the figure no longer implies attention outputs K/V.

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue: The red KV comparison callout is duplicated verbatim under both the Dense 70B and MoE columns: both read “dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB.” Because each callout sits inside a single model column, the layout implies that both columns contain the same two-value comparison rather than assigning 12 GB to the dense model and 0.6 GB to the MoE model. This is especially risky because the figure’s central claim is that the KV difference comes from attention shape, not MoE routing; the duplicated callout visually reinforces the opposite reading.
evidence: Rendered page shows two separate red boxes, one under the Dense 70B column and one under the MoE column, both containing the identical text “dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB.” The caption correctly states “~12 GB vs ~0.6 GB at 9.2K/8-bit” and “the gap is the shape, not the routing,” but the figure itself does not visually assign the values to the correct columns.
acceptance_test: Replace the two duplicated red callouts with either (a) one shared comparison callout spanning both columns, or (b) column-specific labels: “Dense KV ≈ 12 GB” under Dense 70B and “MoE KV ≈ 0.6 GB” under MoE, with a shared note that the difference is due to attention shape, not routing. Re-render and verify that a reader cannot infer that both models have both KV values.

figure: Figure 25.1 — Anatomy of an ADR, and how one ADR supersedes the next
issue: The red dashed supersession arrow runs from the bottom edge of the whole ADR-001 box to the top edge of the whole ADR-002 box, not from the Consequences field to the Context field. The label says 'consequences of ADR-001 become the context of ADR-002', and the caption says 'the Consequences of ADR-001 may become part of the Context of ADR-002', but the drawn endpoints encode whole-record carryover rather than field-level carryover.
evidence: In the rendered figure, the arrow begins below the 'Alternatives' field of ADR-001 and terminates above 'Title & status' in ADR-002. The five fields are individually drawn, so the reader is invited to read field-level relationships; the arrow contradicts that granularity.
acceptance_test: Redraw the arrow so it originates at the 'Consequences' field of ADR-001 and terminates at the 'Context' field of ADR-002, or add short connector stubs from those two fields to the existing arrow. Re-render and confirm the arrow endpoints visibly attach to the named fields, not to the outer box edges.

figure: Figure 26.1 — Workload fingerprints on the six axes
issue: The legend swatches are solid color blocks, while the bars use hatch patterns (diagonal, crosshatch, dots). In grayscale, the solid legend swatches collapse to similar gray values and do not carry the pattern encoding used in the plot, so the legend cannot reliably map categories to bars without color.
evidence: The rendered legend shows three solid squares: blue for 'Long-context RAG Q&A', orange for 'High-throughput chat', green for 'Batch inference'. The corresponding bars are hatched. The chart's own note says 'per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes', but the legend does not preserve the non-color encoding that makes the bars distinguishable in grayscale.
acceptance_test: Add the matching hatch pattern to each legend swatch, or direct-label the three bars in each group. Re-render in grayscale and confirm a reader can map each bar to its category without relying on hue.

figure: Figure A.1 — 2026 frontier MoE extreme sparsity
issue: The x-axis label says 'Active parameters as % of total', but the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next bar is explicitly computed against the 125B backbone only, excluding the 51B n-gram embedding and 4B MTP. The axis label therefore states a denominator that is false for one of the four plotted bars.
evidence: The Qwen bar is labeled '*4.8%' and the right-side annotation says '125B backbone/6B active (+51B n-gram, 4B MTP)'. The footnote says '* Qwen bar = backbone ratio (125B backbone), excluding the 51B n-gram embedding and 4B MTP.' The chart subtitle says 'denominator: vendor-reported / resident total, varies by vendor', but the axis label still reads 'as % of total'.
acceptance_test: Change the x-axis label to 'Active fraction (vendor-defined denominator)' or 'Active parameters as % of stated denominator', and ensure the Qwen bar's denominator is visually distinguished (e.g., by the existing asterisk plus a short in-plot note). Re-render and confirm the axis label no longer asserts a single common denominator.

issue: The GLM KV-cache scope label is ambiguous and inconsistent with the caption: the table says 'BF16 / layer' under KV cache, while the caption says GLM rows are 'per-layer/per-head scope'. 'BF16' is a precision, not a scope, and 'per head' is missing from the KV label.
evidence: Figure A.2, GLM-5.3-Flash row: '100%→~23% BF16 / layer'; caption: 'GLM’s rows are per-layer/per-head scope, not total FLOPs or total cache.'
acceptance_test: Change the KV label to an explicit scope such as 'per-layer/per-head KV (BF16)' or 'KV per layer/head, BF16'; verify the caption and figure use the same scope wording.

issue: The green model name and green italic scope annotations are low-contrast on white, especially at print size and in grayscale. 'GLM-5.3-Flash', 'BF16 / layer', and 'attention only per head / layer' are rendered in a light green that is difficult to read.
evidence: Figure A.2, GLM row: green text on white; the green annotations are small italic. In grayscale, the green collapses to light gray.
acceptance_test: Darken the green or use black/dark-gray text with a green marker; verify small-text contrast ≥4.5:1 and legibility in a grayscale print proof.

issue: The figure claims to show 'layering' but visually encodes a chronological stack: bars are ordered by ascending dates, the title says 'From a single model to a whole system', and there are no substrate/containment relationships. The caption's disclaimer that it is 'not a causal lineage' is doing work the visual should do.
evidence: Figure A.3 bars: Transformer ~2017, Efficient Transformer ~2020, MoE Transformer ~2022, ... Agent Fleet ~2026; caption: 'vertical stacking is a layering ... not a causal lineage'.
acceptance_test: Either redraw as an explicit layered/substrate diagram with containment or dependency cues, or relabel the figure as a chronology and remove the 'layering' claim; test that a reader can state the intended relationship without reading the caption.

issue: White labels on the light blue and light green bars have insufficient contrast: 'Inside test-time search', 'Inside post-training', and 'Inside weights' are hard to read at print size and nearly disappear in grayscale.
evidence: Figure A.4: white text on light blue and light green fills; the light fills become light gray in grayscale.
acceptance_test: Darken those fills or switch to dark text; verify small-text contrast ≥4.5:1 and a grayscale print proof.

issue: The binary legend 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' implies exclusive placement, while the caption says the bands are 'nonexclusive placement choices'. The color coding can make readers treat system-side and model-side as mutually exclusive categories.
evidence: Figure A.4 legend: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'; caption: 'nonexclusive placement choices, not a ranking'.
acceptance_test: Change the legend to 'system-side emphasis' / 'model-side emphasis' or use a gradient/annotation that shows overlap; test that a reader can explain nonexclusive placement from the figure alone.

issue: The recurrent-state row draws three separate fixed-size state boxes side by side ('state after t1', 'state after t2', 'state after t3'), which visually implies three simultaneously retained states. The caption says 'Successive state snapshots, not jointly retained history', but the diagram's layout works against that correction.
evidence: The upper row shows three distinct red state boxes at the same vertical level, each labeled 'fixed-size state'. The caption explicitly says 'Successive state snapshots, not jointly retained history' and 'recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained.' The visual still reads as three retained snapshots unless the reader carefully parses the caption.
acceptance_test: Redraw the recurrent-state row as a single state box updated in place across t1/t2/t3, or use ghosted/replacement arrows that make clear each state replaces the previous one. The figure should be unambiguous without relying on the caption sentence 'not jointly retained history'.

issue: The caption says 'The same 70B model serves in ~165 GB (weights + KV, max 9.5K — canonical input 9.2K)', but the bar is labeled 'Inference (weights+KV)' and the note says activation, microbatch/sequence, and offload/checkpointing are NOT included. The phrase 'serves in ~165 GB' can be read as a full deployment footprint rather than a conditional floor.
evidence: Bar label: 'Inference (weights+KV) ~165 GB'. Note below chart: 'Each bar is a conditional floor (weights + the listed states), not a full deployment config. Activation, microbatch/sequence, and offload/checkpointing are NOT included (Table 7-2).' Caption: 'The same 70B model serves in ~165 GB (weights + KV, max 9.5K — canonical input 9.2K) ...'
acceptance_test: Change the caption to say 'has a weights+KV floor of ~165 GB' rather than 'serves in ~165 GB', and ensure the bar label or caption explicitly says 'floor, not full deployment footprint'. The reader should not be able to infer that 165 GB is sufficient for a production serving configuration.

issue: The KV band's request-slot boundaries are not visually distinguishable from the decorative dot fill. The caption says faint vertical rules mark the 24.9 GB request slots, but at print size the reader cannot count or see 17 full slots plus the half slot; the figure therefore does not visually support the concurrency arithmetic it is meant to explain.
evidence: The orange KV band is filled with a regular white-dot grid. The caption claims 'faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots,' but the vertical dot columns blend into the horizontal dot rows. The equation below gives 17.5 slots, yet the bar does not visibly encode 17.5 divisions.
acceptance_test: Redraw the KV band with distinct, thin vertical slot boundaries (17 full slots plus one half-slot), remove or suppress the competing dot grid, and verify at 100% print size and in grayscale that a reader can count the slots and see the half-slot.

issue: The color legend contradicts the figure's central distinction. Shared memory, L2 cache, and registers are storage resources but are colored blue, which the legend labels 'compute.' Conversely, 'other GPUs / remote' is colored green, which the legend labels 'interconnect,' even though it denotes a remote device/resource rather than a link. The single vertical stack and red gradient arrow also reinforce a one-ladder reading that the caption explicitly denies.
evidence: Legend: blue = compute, orange = memory, green = interconnect. But 'shared mem (SRAM)' and 'L2 cache' are blue; 'registers' is blue; 'other GPUs / remote' is green. The caption says compute, memory, and interconnect are 'separate groups within this stack, not levels of one ladder,' yet the figure draws one continuous vertical stack with one red 'capacity grows / speed drops / distance grows' arrow spanning all categories.
acceptance_test: Recolor by resource type: compute units, on-chip memory, off-chip memory, interconnect, and remote device. Separate the groups visually (e.g., parallel columns or brackets) and restrict the gradient arrow to the memory hierarchy. Verify that the legend matches every box and that the figure remains interpretable in grayscale.

issue: The legend says blue = data/state and orange = compute, but UMT5-XXL and VAE encode are compute modules and are colored blue. This makes the visual encoding inconsistent with the legend and obscures which boxes are computation versus data.
evidence: Legend: 'Blue: data/state. Orange: compute.' The 'UMT5-XXL ≤512 prompt tokens' box and the 'VAE encode I2V condition only' box are blue, although both are neural-network compute modules. By contrast, 'Wan2.2 dense TI2V-5B + scheduler' and 'VAE decode' are orange.
acceptance_test: Recolor UMT5-XXL and VAE encode as compute (orange), or introduce and label a third category such as 'conditioning encoder' with its own legend entry. Verify that every box's color matches its role and that the legend explains all colors used.

issue: Panel B's pipeline-bubble annotation is a text line flush against the panel's left border and no bubble region is drawn; the caption says the panel shows 'an idle bubble at fill/drain'.
evidence: The line 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain — pipeline-wide' begins at the panel border (first glyph at the border, no inset) and sits below three GPU boxes with no shaded or dashed idle region. Caption: 'pipeline parallel splits the layer stack into stages (hidden states move P2P; an idle bubble at fill/drain)'.
acceptance_test: Redraw panel B with a visible bubble region (e.g., dashed idle slots at pipeline fill/drain) and inset the annotation by at least one text-height from the panel border; verify at print size that no glyph is clipped and that the bubble is visually distinguishable from the stage boxes.
